note: The ForeverRank Database: everything shared about Warcraft Forever, compiled. Sources credited in SOURCES on GitHub. To be checked against the beta client once it opens on Sept 17.

facts: One Legacy Point per challenge completed; roughly 65 earnable at launch.
Points are account-wide across rulesets. The Hardcore block is one-way: Hardcore progress and Legacy points carry out to the other rulesets, nothing carries in.
Each character spends up to 16 points, separately, across three account trees.
Trees at launch: Adventure, Resourcefulness and Professions, 7 perks each. Nothing in them is combat throughput; Dedicated Study is the one active ability.
Grew out of the team's favourite parts of Hardcore: the journey, not the destination.
Per the Destin interview, the Legacy system exists to encourage alts: each new playthrough starts a little easier.
Demo characters carried 13 and 31 Legacy points at BlizzCon, well past the 16-per-character launch cap, so the demo did not enforce it.
Changes are staged and committed with Apply Changes, the way retail talent loadouts work; right-click unlearns.
Blizzard plans new challenges, perks, higher caps, new columns inside the existing trees and possibly whole new trees.
Hardcore gets its own Legacy challenges and perks.

legacy.treeNote: 21 perks across three account-wide trees, 7 each, plus two future-patch placeholder slots per tree whose tooltip reads "To be added in future patch content". Each character can spend 16 Legacy points at launch (the seasonal cap), with 65 earnable and more columns, perks and trees planned. Perk names, ranks, positions and rank texts come from beta client build 1.60.1.69876.
legacy.tierRule: Column 1 is open from the first point; everything to its right was locked at 0 spent and open by 5 in the demo footage, so this calculator asks 5 points in that tree. A line means the node needs the one it hangs off maxed: Frequent Flier opened only once Field Guide hit 3 of 3.
legacy.availTip: You can spend up to your current seasonal cap of 16 Legacy Points in total.
rewards: Toy: stun other holders and keep score
legacy.rewardsNote: The Legacy Reward Track counts points earned, not points spent, so every challenge past your 16 still pays out. Thresholds read from in-game captures; one fansite lists the pet at 23.
challenges: Player vs. Player: Ranks, Reputations, Season Journey

Paladin: Changed. It no longer eats your seal. 10 yd range, 10 sec cooldown. Judging Seal of Fury taunts for 4 sec, so Paladins can tank pulls now.
The tank seal. Every hit adds Holy damage, and with a shield up you get an absorb worth half of it. Rank 4 by level 38.
Baseline Ret strike on a 12 sec cooldown: weapon damage plus Holy. Rank 5 by 38. Several talents build on it.
Both trainable now, not talents. Consecration comes at level 20.
Changed: full damage and threat on up to four targets, then reduced damage and threat on anything beyond those four.

Per Blizzard's notes: Improved Holy Strike cuts its cooldown, Voice of Truth gives brief Silence and interrupt immunity, and Reverence lets Spirit regen Mana while casting. Infusion of Light makes Holy Shock and Flash of Light crits speed up Holy Light, and Holy Shock moves to a 10 sec cooldown. Consecrated Ground makes enemies in Consecration take more Holy damage, and Light's Vigil is a costly cooldown that can reset Holy Shock.

Improved Seal of Fury returns Mana when the seal absorbs damage and Shield Specialization returns Mana on blocks. Swift Judgment resets Judgment once a minute, so a missed taunt isn't the end. Templar's Bulwark is a big max-health absorb tied to Forbearance, Reckoning now also procs from blocks, and Iron Creed makes timed Holy Strikes cut incoming damage briefly.

Vindication lowers the enemy's attack power and raises yours, Sacred Arbiter strengthens Holy Strike and renews Judgments on the target, Champion of the Light scales spell damage with Intellect, Instrument of the Law cuts threat and makes Holy Wrath instant, and Twist of Light supports seal twisting. Paladins still get no interrupt and no slow.
Priest: Execute-style Shadow spell. Named by the Early Demise talent.
A normal Shadow spell now, not an Undead racial. Rank 3 by 38, 1 min cooldown.
Every Priest gets it. 3 min cooldown.
Hunter: Trainable now instead of a Marksmanship talent, and quicker: 2 sec cast, 6 sec cooldown, shared with Multi-Shot (Classic was a 3 sec cast). Rank 3 by 38. A reader caught the cast time on Xaryu's stream.
Call Pet is named after your pet. The demo Hunter's read Call Owl.
Changed. Rank 1 makes you untrackable and adds 50 melee attack power. Classic was untrackable only. Spotted by a reader on Xaryu's stream.
Mage: New little ability: decipher an untranslated scroll. Seen on a Skyborne Mage.
A bolt that is both Fire and Frost. Four talents mention it.
Warlock: Enslave Demon under its newer name, which Classic Era now uses too. Rank 1 by 38.
Curse of Agony, renamed. Bane of Doom the same. Banes and Curses are now separate, so you can run one of each.
Male counterpart to the Succubus with its own Summon Incubus spell in the Demonology book, and four Demonology talents name it. Not new against today's Classic Era, which added it in patch 1.14.4.
Warrior: Baseline. It sits in the Arms tab of the demo spellbook.
A passive in the Arms tab now, not a talent.
Still in the game: the Fury tree has Improved Intercept. It just isn't in the level 38 spellbook, so it's probably learned later than 30 now.
Rank 3 by 38 (Classic reached that at 46) and it has a 15 sec cooldown now.
Changed. Works in Battle or Defensive Stance. Rank 4 slows attacks 20% for 22 sec and hits up to 4 targets, where Classic was 10% for 30. Read off Xaryu's stream, thanks to a reader.
Still there, in the Protection tab. 116 health for 10 rage plus 10 more over 10 sec.

Changed: 15 min cooldown, 60% less damage for 12 sec (Classic was 30 min, 75% for 10 sec). In Esfand's video it was ready while Retaliation was on cooldown, so the shared cooldown with Retaliation and Recklessness looks gone. Two readers flagged this.
Rogue: Rogues can use one-handed axes now. The Hack and Slash talent lists Axe/Sword as a weapon group.
Druid: Omen of Clarity and Nature's Grasp
Both trainable now, not talents. They're in the Balance tab at 38.
New out-of-combat resurrection, 10 sec cast. Rebirth keeps its 30 min cooldown.
Bear bleed from later expansions, in Forever as a baseline ability: the Shredding Attacks talent cuts its Rage cost. Not in the level 38 spellbook, so it comes later. Thanks to a reader.
Gone. Abolish Poison is the only poison cure.
Shaman: Half a second faster than Classic. Rank 7 is a 2.5 sec cast.
Also half a second faster: rank 1 is a 2 sec cast, 6 sec cooldown, 3 targets, each jump 30% weaker. Max Elemental Alacrity brings Lightning Bolt to the same 2 sec.
New: move your totems to you. Totemic Recall is in too.
New: drops up to four totems from your Totem Bar in one 3 sec cast.
The tooltip no longer says outdoors only: 100 mana, instant, 40% speed, and that is the whole text. Read on Guzu's stream.

A spell now, not a totem: 30 yd range, instant, 10 sec cooldown, and it blasts everything within 10 yd of your active Fire totem (rank 3 does 206 to 231 at 38). Improved Fire Nova trims 2 sec off the cooldown. Read on Esfand's stream.

Priest.note: From the BlizzCon demo. Fear Ward is now baseline for every Priest. Night Elf and Troll spells read from level 38 spellbook tooltips.

Undead: Instant, 10 min cooldown. Cannibalize 720 of your own Health over 15 sec to gain 720 Mana. (Rank 2, level 38 values.)
Troll: Changed. Rank 3: 45 mana, instant, 30 yd. Reduces the target's melee attack power by 85 and the effectiveness of healing on it by 20% for 2 min. (Classic reduced flat melee damage instead of attack power.)
Rank 3: 30 mana, instant. Shadows strike anyone who hits you with a spell, melee or ranged attack for 76 Shadow damage, once every few seconds, no threat. 3 charges, lasts 10 min.
Dwarf: Holy damage plus a short root, as in TBC.
Instantly heals you, as in TBC.
Gnome: Rank 2 at 38: 220 mana, instant, 30 yd, 10 min cooldown. Places a Holy ward on an ally for 15 sec; the next hit that drops them below 35% health gives them a 290 absorb and heals 338 over 15 sec. One Contingency Plan per target. Read from a demo spellbook tooltip.
Human: Cooldown that removes Weakened Soul from the target and heals them.
Night Elf: Changed. Instant, 26 mana, 5 min cooldown: reduces the chance you will be hit by melee and ranged attacks by 50% for 15 sec or until you are missed 3 times. (Classic: ranged only, plus dodge, 3 min cooldown.) Read from the demo spellbook at level 38.

Changed. Rank 4 at 38: 190 mana, 30 yd, channeled, 30 sec cooldown. Rains starshards on the target for 816 Arcane damage over 6 sec. (Classic: no cooldown and far less damage.) Read from a demo spellbook tooltip.

facts: No server realms: four rule-set ecosystems (Normal, PvP, Roleplaying, Hardcore), each one large world.
No cross-ruleset grouping; factions stay separate.
Two-part character names (first and last), unique per region.
Language preference matchmaking.
No level scaling anywhere; the cap stays 60 and zones keep their levels.
Everyone starts at level 1 on launch day; the beta opens at cap 20 and rises to 30, where it stays for the whole beta.
On the Normal ruleset, PvP only happens by mutual consent. The Season of Discovery-style faction-balance levers are named for the PvP ruleset specifically.
Both names are required at character creation, but a setting decides whether the second one is shown.

The shop lists these languages: English (US and EU), Spanish (Latin America and EU), Brazilian Portuguese, German, French, Russian, Korean and Traditional Chinese. Regions: Americas and Oceania, Europe, Korea, Taiwan.
Patches roll out region by region at off-peak times, as in modern WoW. Asked about Steam, Ion Hazzikostas said the subscription model makes Battle.net the better fit for now.

Meeting Stones sit at dungeon entrances but cannot summon; they open a Looking for Group listing tool. Nothing forms groups or teleports you, so a Warlock is the only summon, and the designers call the walk deliberate social time.
Arrives after launch as a sealed ecosystem with its own progression.
Dead Hardcore characters can transfer OUT to other rulesets.
Collections and Legacy Points never transfer IN.
Mak'gora got a tease: the team is thinking about ways to run Mak'gora tournaments in the future, with nothing promised yet.
A new check asks you to confirm you are in a safe spot before a world refresh. Warcraft Tavern says it applies to every ruleset, not only Hardcore.
The team says it built Forever with Hardcore players in mind: new special-effect items make dungeon runs worth the risk, and the Legacy system is meant to be especially useful to Hardcore players.
Six new race and class pairings: Gnome Priest, Human Hunter, Dwarf Shaman, Orc Mage, Troll Warlock and Undead Paladin.
Every race now carries two active and two passive racial abilities; the full set was catalogued from the demo.
The Skyborne bring a glide racial, and their race plus the Zephras Isle start sit behind the paid Heroic Pack.

Skyborne come in two versions, picked at character creation: High Order (Alliance) and Windshaper (Horde). Both get Walk on Air (10 sec glide), Wind Blessed (+1% haste) and Elemental Insight (+5% damage against Elementals); High Order add Read Ley Line (+100% Health and Mana regen), Windshapers add Skysight (+10% run speed).
Skyborne Druids get their own sky-blue Bear, Cat, bird Travel and Moonkin forms; no Tree form has been shown. The race also has its own voices and dances, plus skin tones that aren't blue.
Talent trees keep Classic's row count and the 11, 21 and 31-point milestone talents, and add a new milestone at 16 points.
No Season of Discovery-style role bending (Shaman tanks and the like) at launch. Classes start from Classic-level simplicity, though the designers say the conversation stays open.

Blizzard's own examples. Dwarf: Stoneform reduces Physical damage instead of adding armor, Find Treasure stays up alongside other tracking, Mace Specialization adds crit, Big Game Hunter adds damage against Beasts. Undead: Will of the Forsaken still breaks Charm, Fear and Sleep but lost its immunity, Cannibalize also restores Mana, Underwater Breathing is unchanged, and the new Touch of the Grave drains life on hit.

No racial raises weapon skill any more. Gun Specialization, Bow and Throwing Specialization and the Human Mace Specialization are gone, while Human Sword and Orc Axe Specialization now add crit. The weapon skill tooltip now shows its effect against the target's level.

More racials read from the demo: Tauren Cultivation grows herb nodes anyone can gather, Orc Shatter Curse, Gnome Eureka! (next 3 spells cheaper and 10% stronger) and Expansive Mind (+5% max Mana, Rage and Energy), Human Will to Survive and Perception. Fansite transcriptions disagree on the durations.
Modern and Classic visual presets, with HD and SD character models and restored Classic animations on the HD set.

Official gamepad support: an Xbox controller sat at the BlizzCon demo stations, driving an alpha-stage mode that navigates the UI with radial menus. The Skyborne 1-10 demo supported it; the dungeon demo did not.
Character creation asks for the two-part name up front, and the map tracks several quests at once instead of one.
Computational in-combat add-ons, such as automated marking and callouts, will be restricted as in modern WoW, and there is no one-button rotation.

Blizzard Watch says the first-login choice reads Classic or Enhanced: Classic means old models, a map without quest objectives, and transmog off; Enhanced turns on HD models, map objectives, transmog and a single combined bag. Blizzard's recap calls them modern and Classic presets, so the exact labels are unconfirmed.
The Barbershop is in and working.

Rendering: volumetric fog with sun shafts, true sun and moon shadows, global illumination from a custom ray tracer that runs even on minimum spec, and flowing water with foam and reflections. Draw distance is longer too: the Wetlands has a view of Dun Morogh, and of Dalaran's towers toward Alterac.
Artists rebuilt the lighting zone by zone, using the original 1.12 client as reference, and new art keeps to the Vanilla style rather than modern WoW's.
Burning Crusade model: the mount comes free with riding training; the training carries the cost.
No flying mounts. A design pillar, not an oversight.
Forsaken Paladin mounts previewed (the Undead Paladin rides something suitably dead).
Forsaken Paladins start their story at Bandarion Keep in Tirisfal's Whispering Wood, picking up from the Warcraft III Forsaken Kingdom campaign, and get a dedicated epic mount quest at 60.
600+ new recipes across professions and level bands; Advanced Blueprints drop from dungeon bosses.
Campfires become camps: up to three crafted objects (5-10 when a Cook upgrades it), one per player, one-hour cooldown.

Camp objects per profession: Sharpening Wheel (BS, Attack Power), Faction Banner (Tailor, Spirit), Incense Candle (Herbalist, Intellect), First Aid Kit (First Aid, Stamina on par with Power Word: Fortitude, made from Linen Bandages and Refreshing Spring Water), Alchemy Lab, Tanning Rack. Blacksmiths can also place an Anvil and a Master Forge.
Every cooked food's Well Fed buff also adds 5% experience from kills. Sitting at the fire is mandatory and correct.
An upgraded campsite offers rest, vendors and repairs on top of the profession workspaces and their one-hour buffs.

Each profession has three camp objects learned at different skill levels. The first comes at skill 20, from camping NPCs or trainers; the advanced ones come from Blueprints that drop from dungeon bosses.
Camp buffs are variants of class buffs and don't stack with them.
First Aid now makes curatives (Woolen Tourniquet for bleeds, Simple Poultice for diseases, Anti-Venom for poisons) and healing potions, in a retail-style profession window.

A new market at Three Corners in Redridge houses the Azeroth Commerce Authority, Season of Discovery's Waylaid Supplies faction; its Horde twin is Durotar Supply and Logistics. It pays in a new currency, Merchant's Favor. Marcy Baker takes crate turn-ins, and Tamelyn Aldridge sells a tabard, supply packs and an Advertising License Application that starts a quest for a Dwarven Tradeskill Sign toy.

The market has a vendor for each profession. Seen so far: 29 new Alchemy recipes (thrown AoE smog potions, damage-over-time potions, 30-second combat potions, 30-minute elixirs) and 6 Cooking smoothies that grant Spirit.

Enchanting gets 40 new items: Druid idols, Paladin librams and Shaman totems for the relic slot, craftable staves, a wand, held-in-off-hand items, necklace enchants and an off-hand enchant. Some need new materials such as dyes.
Each crafting profession has a certification item that unlocks a title, usable only at 300 skill.
Hit and crit are unified across spell, melee and ranged.
Bonus healing carries one-third bonus damage; caster weapons roll spell power. Bonus healing and damage show up on gear from level 10.
Expertise is the new stat that reduces enemy parry and dodge. Weapon-skill items are nerfed from auto-best: the Deep Dive slide showed Edgemaster's Handguards cut from +7 to +1 weapon skill.
Environment-keyed item effects (Woodlands, Mountains, Deserts) and creature-type effects.
Hundreds of new rare-creature and dungeon drops; unique dungeon boss items are blue.

Baseline buffs: Blessing of Kings, Divine Spirit and Improved Mark of the Wild are trained, not talented, per the panel. The current demo transcriptions agree: all three are gone from the talent trees, and Kings and Divine Spirit sit in the demo spellbooks.

Items actually named so far: Worgenbane Talisman (trinket, conditional against Worgen), Tidal Charm (conditional against Naga and their kin), Graverobber's Shovel (zone-bound utility), Whitemane's Chapeau (healer piece, upgraded from its Classic self), Sharpened Cutlery (shown, undetailed), Ladimore Heirloom Ring (caster ring from Duskwood's Mor'ladim quest), Master Hunter's Spellsword (from Nesingwary's quests), Edgemaster's Handguards (the weapon-skill example above).
No full tooltips have been published for any of them, which is why the Forge refuses to offer gear until the beta.
Set bonuses and world-drop epics were reworked.
Pacing target: an ordinary mob takes a solo player about 10 to 15 seconds to kill, and crowd control and threat are meant to matter in dungeons.
Configured in cities; Classic Mode switches it all off at launch.
Uncommon/Rare BoP dungeon drops teach their look to every eligible looter; raid epics only to the winner.
Type rules hold (cloth stays cloth); low levels cannot wear 60 looks, but every level limit on appearances lifts once you hit 60. Helm and cloak can be hidden even with transmog switched off.
Poor and Common items grant their appearance on loot without binding, and you keep collecting while transmog is off. Cosmetic-only items will be rare.
The honor system is reworked; thresholds, decay and caps unpublished until the beta or a blue post.
Earning PvP ranks is one of the six Legacy Challenge categories: each rank challenge pays a Legacy Point.
For Great Honor, a Resourcefulness Legacy perk, grants +2% honor per rank.
Honorable kills pay by the victim's rank; battleground objectives pay on top.
PvP season refreshes scheduled Spring 2027 and Summer 2027.
Honor from battlegrounds and other PvP climbs a rank ladder. Rank 14 is reachable within a single season or patch cycle, and rewards include cosmetics and stat-bearing PvP armor.
PvP gear appearances unlock for transmog only once you hold the rank the gear requires.
The original Vanilla battlegrounds stay, with Darkspear Islands added alongside.
The full dated plan lives in the Roadmap section below.
Positioned as evergreen: expanding this Azeroth over time rather than expiring it.

Expansion is horizontal and stays on Azeroth for the foreseeable future: unfinished and unused zones get fleshed out rather than new continents bolted on. Chris Metzen works with the quest and lore team daily.
Blizzard rules nothing out for the long term, new classes included.
Blizzard's four design pillars: approachable and familiar, the world as the main character, the journey before the destination, and protecting the social experience.
Included with a normal WoW subscription or Game Time; no separate base purchase.
Paid upgrades add: the Skyborne race and its zone, cosmetics, early name reservation, beta access, Game Time or Warcraft III content by tier.

Physical Collector's Edition via the Gear Store, while supplies last: $150 per Blizzard Watch, with a 13-inch Dwarf and Bear statue, a Zephras Isle mousepad, art prints, pins, a companion journal and a Warcraft Forever Collection code. Blizzard Watch saw it listed as sold out on Sept 13.
No WoW Token and no boosts, and no plans for either: "The Journey is the game," per associate production director Clay Stone in Destin's BlizzCon interview.
US shop prices: Skyborne Heroic Pack $29.99, Skyborne Epic Pack $59.99, Warcraft Forever Collection $79.99.
Euro and pound prices, per Mobalytics and not yet seen on a Blizzard page: Heroic €29.99 or £25.99, Epic €59.99 or £51.99, Collection €79.99 or £69.99.

Heroic Pack: the Skyborne race and Zephras Isle, the Cerulean Prideclaw mount (riding training not included), Shen'dorei Skyseer's Garb, Veteran Adventurer's Rucksack, the Shen'dorei Windwell toy, Skyborne housing decor for modern WoW, early name reservation and one Invite-A-Friend code. The mount, transmog and toy work in both modern WoW and Forever.

Epic Pack adds beta access, 30 days of Game Time (credited from Nov 4), the Veteran Adventurer's Loyal Companion mount and Outdoor Wear set, Zergling, Panda, Diablo and Pachimari pets, and Lordaeron and Shen'dorei tabards; the pets and tabards are Forever-only. The Collection adds Warcraft III: Reforged, the Forsaken Kingdom campaign, and Forsaken and Human figurine decor.

Invite-A-Friend launch codes: one with Heroic, three with Epic, three with the Collection. They go out by email from Oct 20 and let a friend play Forever free from Nov 4 to 11. Gift purchases are excluded.
The Warcraft Forever Collection is sold only through Jan 11, 2027. None of the bundled in-game items work in WoW Classic.
Bought a digital edition before your Collector's Edition arrives? Redeem the CE code by Dec 31, 2027 and you may get Battle.net Balance credit; not every product qualifies.

Minimum PC: Windows 10 64-bit (May 2019 update), a 4-core 3.0 GHz CPU (Intel Haswell or AMD Zen), a DirectX 12 GPU with 4 GB (GTX 10 series, RDNA 1 or Intel Iris Xe2 Lunar Lake), 8 GB RAM, an SSD with 128 GB free, 1280x720. Icy Veins lists a higher minimum CPU (6-core Coffee Lake or Zen 2); the shop page is Blizzard's own.
Recommended PC: Windows 11, 8 performance cores at 5.2 GHz boost (Core Ultra Series 2 or Ryzen Zen 5), a DirectX 12 GPU with 8 GB (RTX 40, RDNA 3 or Arc B-Series), 16 GB RAM, a 128 GB SSD.
Mac minimum: macOS 12, Apple M2 or 9th-gen Intel Coffee Lake, a Metal GPU with 4 GB, 8 GB RAM, a 128 GB SSD. Recommended: macOS 15, Apple M4, 16 GB RAM.
Blizzard said on the WoW UI Discord that Midnight's addon restrictions, including secret values, will be active in Forever, so Classic-era addons such as WeakAuras will not simply carry over.

Forever shares modern WoW's UI code and most of the patch 12.1.5 addon API, and the AuraContainer and AuraButton changes from 12.1.0 come with it; future UI changes are expected to land in both games.
Internally Forever is a separate game type in the modern WoW code called Camelot, a name Blizzard says will change before launch.
Familiar Faces, shown by lead software engineer Ana Resendez in the Deep Dive panel, tries to place you in the same world copy as players you have met before and keeps guildmates together.
The world refresh warning is a 3-minute countdown with a button to move now if you are already safe; principal designer Kris Zierhut said it was built for Hardcore but is in the whole game.
The BlizzCon demo showed a fifth bag slot that only takes a reagent bag.
Josh Greenfield said the default bank is much larger, around 96 slots, while starting bags stay at Classic size.
A mounts window keeps mounts out of your bags.
Item stats are hidden in the game files: an item's stats only show once it has dropped for you or someone on your server, so best-in-slot lists and raid loot will not be known ahead of launch.
There is no dungeon journal at first, so boss abilities stay unknown until players fight them.
Blizzard says the world is full of hidden secrets, but unlike Season of Discovery they do not lock away player power.
Josh Greenfield said each camp object lasts about 10 minutes and has a one-hour cooldown, and a campfire must be placed a certain distance from other campfires so shanty towns do not form.
A Fish Bowl camp object that buffs all stats is among the camp objects shown so far.
Placing a higher-tier camp object replaces the buff from a lower-tier version.
In The Sun interview, developers said Molten Core will open some day, but not at launch; they wanted to start with something new.
Skyborne class options: both factions can be Warriors, Hunters, Rogues and Druids; Alliance (High Order) Skyborne can also be Mages and Horde (Windshaper) Skyborne can also be Shamans.
Talent trees have 7 rows with 5 points per row, and each tree has four one-point talents (at 11, 16, 21 and 31 points). The goal is to make all 27 talent trees viable in dungeons and raids.
Josh Greenfield said wilder Season of Discovery roles such as Warlock or Shaman tanks are not in yet, but he would never say never.
In the fansite talent calculators, Combat Rogue finishers lower other cooldowns, much like the Outlaw Rogue's Restless Blades.
Every raid boss has a rare chase item that is very strong, at about the level of Dragonspine Trophy in TBC, so level 60 raids stay worth doing.
Tier set pieces can drop in all three raid sizes (10, 20 and 40), and item power is meant to rise more slowly so older raids stay relevant.
The September 17 live Q&A starts with modern WoW at 10:00 a.m. PDT, and the Forever segment follows at 10:30 a.m. PDT.
McDonald's Australia gives a Forever beta key for 1,000 MyMacca's points: one per MyMacca's account and per WoW account, while stocks last, redeemable by October 20, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. AEDT.
Per the McDonald's promotion terms, you need a Battle.net account but no WoW subscription or game time to play the beta.
The McDonald's promotion FAQ says beta character progress will not carry over to launch, and fansites say the same; Blizzard itself has still not said so in a post.
The beta cap never goes above 30, so no raids can be tested in the beta.

In the Battle.net launcher, Forever has its own entry in the game version dropdown and must be installed separately. With beta access, the date under the Install button reads September 17, 2026; without it, it reads November 4, 2026.
Blizzard's Carve a New Path post gives the launch as 3:00 p.m. PDT on November 4, while the shop says PST. Daylight saving time ends on November 1, so the launch falls on PST (UTC-8).
Kotaku reports that the Forever Collector's Edition is being heavily scalped.

Blizzard's public patch service lists two encrypted internal builds on a new 1.60 version line: 1.60.1.69800 (product wowdev2, labelled World of Warcraft Classic Alpha) and 1.60.0.69818 (wowdev5). Their game data is encrypted and cannot be read, and nothing yet confirms they are Forever.
A new product code, wowf, exists on Blizzard's patch service with a CDN entry but no build yet; it may be the Forever beta or client, but that is unconfirmed.
As of September 16 no Forever build is public: wago.tools lists only retail, PTR and existing Classic builds, the newest being 12.1.5.69848 on the 12.1.5 PTR.
The Engineering schematic vendor at the Azeroth Commerce Authority market is Fritz Fizzle; most schematics cost 42 in the market currency.
The Tailoring pattern vendor is Mivin Shadowweave; patterns cost 11 and the Tailoring Certification costs 80 in the market currency.
New crafting materials named in the recipes: Azerothium Bar, Legionite Bar, Torbernite, Marefoil, plus Viridian, Magenta and Cerulean Dye.
Engineering gets Wrath-style Tinkers, including a 20-yard teleport and Nitro Boosts. They are built from a new Tinkerbox reagent, and the Tinker schematics require Engineering 280.

SAF-T devices such as the Disposable Parachute and the Emergency Field Cloak have charges, which the Ultrasafe Rechargeable Battery restores. Most new engineering gear has no Engineering requirement to use, except the Stealthman 52 and the Ultralight Goblin Glider, which need Engineering 250.

All new Tailoring recipes make bind-on-equip items usable by non-tailors: cloth pieces with spell-school damage or healing (required levels 12 to 50) and two reagent bags, a 12-slot Mageweave and a 14-slot Runecloth.
Two engineering recipes are marked NYI (not yet implemented): the Interdimensional Companion Repository and the Gnomish Weather Machine.

zones: Skyborne starting zone, levels 1-12. The shen'dorei trace back to rebels who left Eldre'Thalas after the War of the Ancients and settled in Skywall; now their elemental patrons are gone, the pylons holding the isle together are failing, and the Windshapers, High Order and Al'Aketh fight over it. The demo route starts at Thendal Village in the northwest and loops south and around past the Shrine of Alar and fog-choked Shadowgate Forest, with a sleeping Altarius in the Ruins of Ban'aethal to the northeast and crane-like galestriders roaming.

Eastern Kingdoms, levels 30-45, the missing mid-game band: previously unreachable land about the size of Stranglethorn, bordering the Burning Steppes, Redridge, the Swamp of Sorrows and the Badlands. Nearly 200 quests, Powderfuse Port as the landing for the Steamwheedle ship, and Powderfuse goblins, Twilight's Hammer, the Brotherhood of the Horse, gnolls and ogres.
Post-Archimonde Hyjal, Darkwhisper Gorge and a recovering world tree. An endgame levelling zone with new reputations and emerging factions, and home to one of the Barrow Deeps' three entrances.

A new area south of Desolace, reached through the Valley of Bones. It explores the Shen'dralar of Eldre'Thalas (Dire Maul) and a war between centaur tribes, and gives new reasons to visit Maraudon and Razorfen Downs.
dungeons: Levels 13-18, beneath Ironforge. Royal dwarven burial chambers disturbed by Dark Iron infiltrators; undead and ghost-haunted corridors. Alliance-flavoured; Horde entry takes trickery.
Levels 15-20, above Undercity. Reclaim the devastated city from lingering Scourge; a necromancer preparing another attack is the final boss. Horde-flavoured; Alliance get safe passage.
Levels 24-29, Wetlands, above Whelgar's Excavation; Blizzard's dungeon list calls it Excavation Site: Wetlands. Explorer's League dig with a mysterious purpose, and probably raptors.

Levels 28-33, pre-bubble Dalaran. The barrier is down: haywire enchantments, uncontrolled constructs, demonic influence. Doubles as a social hub with vendors and quests, and the city around it is explorable.

Levels 35-40, off Stranglethorn's coast. Ancient troll ruins risen from the sea: trolls, Naga, and stranded pirates. Playable on the BlizzCon floor, where the bosses included Zul'Alai (enrages near death) and Zin'aka, the trash was Makrura, Naga and Risen Troll Sentries, and a shark lurked in the central courtyard pool.

Levels 40-45, the Riverglades. Enormous Ogre dungeon: kidnappings, raids on settlements, Twilight's Hammer cultists and Old God rituals with suspicious nighttime chanting. A blue post fixed the range after an earlier 40-55 listing.
Levels 48-53, Alcaz Island. A prison holding Defias inmates, with Naga pressing in.
Levels 55-60, Azshara. Corrupted furbolg dungeon with a cleansing theme.
Levels 58-60, Un'Goro Crater. Titan facility full of titan mechanisms, possibly with gauntlet-style encounters.
raids: 10-player, maximum level. Illidan's old prison under Hyjal: Night Elf theming, corruption, and dangerous entities, with three entrances around the world, one on Mount Hyjal. Legacy challenge bosses (8): Deepscar Matriarch, Elder Tangleclaw, Khalith the Dreadspinner, Well of Sorrow, Amethrax, Del'lynar Songwood, Ravus and Darlissa, Sonya Darkhallow.

20-player. Ancient elven ruins with demonic influences and, per Blizzard, maybe some other surprises. Tier sets and a legendary reward hang off the two launch raids. Legacy challenge bosses (13): Bandalar, Ancient of Decay, Time-Lost Battalion, Sylvestris Dusksong, Old Gloomlurker, Gharalis the Abyssal, Kathris the Haunted, Anara Chillwind, Elder Minderel, Tracker Stillwind, Council of Thorns, Nythus the Dreadmbound (possibly a typo for Dreambound), The Wild King.
40-player, unlocking Dec 9 with the rest. Announced on the year-one roadmap; the broodmother keeps her classic address in Dustwallow Marsh, and her Legacy challenge still lists her as the only boss.
battlegrounds: 15v15 off Kalimdor: control points plus Arathi-style capture and defend.
facts: All nine new dungeons ship at launch, set in original-world locations.
First new raid unlock lands Dec 9, 2026; later come more raids and a revamped iconic raid Blizzard will not yet name.
Dungeon bosses drop Advanced Blueprints for professions, unique blue items teach transmog looks to every eligible looter, and hundreds of new rare-creature and dungeon drops pad the loot tables.
More than a thousand new quests across the 1-60 journey, spread over the new and reimagined regions.
New ship routes: Stormwind Harbor to Auberdine, Menethil to Southshore to Auberdine, and a Steamwheedle Cartel line from Tanaris to the Riverglades.
Wetlands gets new quests, Desolace's centaur faction quests gain content and faction rewards, and every starting zone gains NPCs, quests, profession hooks and recipes.
Forever is set in Azeroth's Year 1, after Warcraft III: Forsaken Kingdom and before Kazzak reopens the Dark Portal, in its own time bubble apart from modern lore.
Dungeon mob XP is cut sharply while dungeon quest XP is much higher: first runs pay well, repeat grinding doesn't.
Every raid tier gets at least one 10-player and one 20-player raid, sometimes a 40 as well. No flex raiding.
The experience curve is unchanged: reaching level 60 takes the same total experience as in original WoW.
The Riverglades and Shen'dralas sit in the level range where levelling slows down and give an alternative route, and Hyjal covers the stretch just before 60.

The Riverglades lie north of Redridge, so Alliance players will mostly arrive from there. The zone has humans, orcs, ogres, a goblin outpost and a Black Market Auction House, and Steamwheedle Port has a ship to Gadgetzan.
In Shen'dralas, quests send you into the Valley of Bones, the Magram and Gelkis centaur stories continue from Desolace, and the ruins tie into the Dire Maul story.

Blizzard estimates original WoW had about 3,000 to 3,500 quests. Forever adds about 1,000, with 50 to 200 in each of the four new zones, many new quests in the Wetlands and Azshara, and new content from level 5 onward.
Blizzard's announcement sets Forever after Warcraft III Reforged: Forsaken Kingdom and before Molten Core.
The new hand-drawn loading screens show Dalaran on the ground, Silvermoon in the distance, and a living Teldrassil, as well as Mount Hyjal.

The Skyborne lore: rebels fled the Shen'dralar of Eldre'Thalas around 7,300 years before the Dark Portal, and wind elementals lifted part of the land into Skywall to create Zephras Isle. The Skyborne are not high elves.
Chris Metzen told the team to get a little crazy with the new elf race, and he drew the original concept map of Zephras Isle, which was shown in the Found Photographs panel.
The client build the day before beta is 1.60.1.69876; the game type is internally called Camelot.
Zephras Isle is its own map with more than 30 subzones.
No instance called Drowned City exists in the client; the demo dungeon ships under another name.
The Legacy reward track currency is Renown - Legacy Rank, capped at 90; the PvP ladder uses Renown - PvP Rank, capped at 14.

roadmap.title: Beta
items: Cap 20 at open, rising to 30, where it stays for the whole beta.
Beta access comes with the Skyborne Epic Pack ($59.99) and the Warcraft Forever Collection ($79.99). The $29.99 Heroic Pack does not include it, and the free opt-in only gives a chance at a seat.
Blizzard's shop and pre-purchase terms end the beta on Oct 21 (PST); the official roadmap slide prints Oct 22.
To check whether you got in, look for a Forever beta entry in the Battle.net launcher or a welcome email.

A beta code redeems once per WoW game account, and never on an account that already has beta. Collector's Edition buyers get theirs by email; buyers on the forums reported it arriving about an hour after ordering.
Nothing from Blizzard yet says whether beta characters carry over. Fansites assume a wipe, so treat carryover as unconfirmed.
Blizzard's live WoW Q&A on post-BlizzCon questions, Forever included, streams Thursday Sept 17 at 10:00 a.m. PDT on the Warcraft Twitch and YouTube channels, with a VOD to follow.

roadmap.title: Name reservation
items: Early name reservation and character creation for upgraded editions. Two-part names, unique per region: bring a surname.

The window runs Oct 27 to Nov 3 (PST) and comes with any upgrade, the Heroic Pack included. Up to three characters; names go to whoever claims them first, with no guarantee, and the perk covers only the WoW account it was bought for.

roadmap.title: Launch
items: 3:00 pm PST. Everyone starts at level 1. All nine dungeons open on day one.

roadmap.title: Raids unlock
items: The Barrow Deeps (10-player), Hyjal Summit (20-player), and Onyxia's Lair (40-player).
Tier sets and a legendary reward hang off the launch raids.

roadmap.title: Hardcore
items: The sealed one-life ecosystem opens: own progression, nothing in, dead characters may leave.

roadmap.title: First major update
items: Two new raids (10- and 20-player), two new dungeons, new quests and a new playable area, a new legendary questline, and a PvP season refresh.

roadmap.title: Second major update
items: The revamped iconic raid Blizzard will not yet name, a new raid, expanded world content, two more dungeons, another PvP season refresh, and Professions and Legacy updates.
